name: call_library_function_330
description: Calls an Amiga OS library function: it loads the library base from the A4-relative global table, jumps through the negative offset 330, and returns. It takes no arguments and one routine calls it.

name: forward_handler_call_198
description: Handler stub referenced from a data pointer that forwards control to an unnamed routine: it loads a target from the A4-relative global table at the negative offset 198, jumps there, and returns.

name: call_library_function_198
description: Calls an Amiga OS library function through the A4-relative global table at the negative offset 198, with no arguments set up here. Three routines call it, and it returns straight after the jump.

name: call_library_function_456

name: forward_routine_call_294

name: setup_pointer_chain
description: Initialises a three-word block whose address is passed in: it writes the block's own address into its first word, adds four to that word, clears the second word, and stores the original address in the third word. One routine calls it.

name: start_and_dispatch_program
description: Program entry point: it finds the current task and tests one of its fields to choose between a Workbench start path, which calls library routines and returns a status, and a command-line path. The command-line path copies the arguments, splits them on spaces into a word table, and passes the word count and table to another routine.

name: close_library_and_reply
description: Closes a library handle given as its argument, then, if a stored flag is set, forbids task switching and replies to a message before returning the stored result. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: invoke_two_function_pointers
description: Calls two library functions in sequence through pointers at fixed negative offsets from the A6 register, at offsets 384 and then 372, and returns. It takes no arguments and returns no value.

name: open_dos_library_or_alert
description: Opens the dos library by name. If the open succeeds it returns the library handle; otherwise it runs a fixed error sequence, an alert followed by a close call with a fixed code, and returns the stored result.

name: start_workbench_task
description: Starts the workbench task. It checks a second argument for the debug switch, looks up a resident module by name, creates the workbench.task process, exchanges messages with it, and reports an error text when the module cannot be found or the tool cannot be started.

name: compare_null_terminated_strings
description: Compares two null-terminated strings character by character. It returns zero when they are equal, minus one when the first differing character is smaller in the first string, and one otherwise.

name: build_lock_block_list
description: Builds a linked list of small cleared memory blocks from a table of entries. For each entry it allocates an eight-byte block, stores a duplicated lock taken from the entry's second field into it, and links it to the previous block; it returns the head of the list, or the list built so far on failure.

name: pass_params_to_subroutine
description: Calls another routine with a value from a global variable, its own parameter, and the address of an eight-byte stack slot. It returns nothing and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: format_string_and_pass_on
description: Formats text into a 140-byte stack buffer using a formatting function held in a global variable. It then measures the resulting string and, if it is non-empty, passes the parameter, the buffer and the length to another routine.

name: store_byte_through_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of the data register into the byte location addressed by the A3 register and returns. It is a one-instruction body that one unnamed routine calls.

description: The bytes here do not decode as valid instructions, so the decompiler shows only a halt. It has no behaviour of its own.

name: spin_in_infinite_loop
description: Contains only an unconditional infinite loop, with no calls, data accesses or returns, so execution that reaches it never leaves.
